Yes—several papers address parameter importance for selective freezing, including in MLLMs. AWARe explicitly computes activation-based importance scores and dynamically freezes parameters that are important for preserving prior capabilities while letting less important parameters adapt during MLLM fine-tuning, reducing catastrophic forgetting without architecture changes [2]. Model-Dowser also targets MLLMs, but uses a data-free importance probe based on weight magnitudes, input activations, and output sensitivities to preserve high-importance parameters and update the rest [4].

Related but broader work differs in scope or mechanism. Guarded Freezing studies how to choose what to freeze in pretrained models using removal-value or drift-value depending on connectivity, rather than focusing specifically on MLLMs [1]. GRASS estimates layer importance from mean gradient norms to adaptively sample layers for LLM fine-tuning [10], and LayerTracer argues for training shallow layers while freezing deep layers in continued pre-training based on layer sensitivity and stability [5].
